articleTitle: Some design methods of OTA-C and CCII-RC filters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: OTA-C filters and CCII-RC filters using the CCII as the transconductance amplifier are discussed in a unified context. Benefitting from each other in this way, more OTA-C and CCII-RC filter topologies may be generated. In particular, a class of CCII transconductance amplifier (CCIITA) based filter structures may be obtained from well-developed OTA-filters by simple one-to-one substitution of CCIITAs for OTAs in OTA-C filters. The signal flow graph method of OTA-C and CCII-RC filter synthesis is also investigated in the paper with the emphasis that with different structures the same transfer function may be realized not only as the voltage gain, but other types as well, for example current gain. The modified signal flow graphs of general transfer functions given in the paper are more straightforward for circuit realization. The adjoint network method which has been used to transform voltage amplifier filters to current amplifier counterparts is extended to transform transconductance amplifier filters. Both the indirect SFG transformation method and the direct element replacement method are proposed. These methods may be readily used to produce more filter configurations from the known equivalents. The simple transconductor is also accommodated into these methods and a number of new transconductor-grounded capacitor filters are obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of digital adaptive filters in assessing live speech networks
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: An in-service nonintrusive measurement device for monitoring network performance at the 4-wire trunk level is described. The signal processing functions are extensively performed using a digital adaptive filter (DAF) implemented on a Motorola DSP56001 to characterise an unknown echo-path. Original results have shown that network parameters can be derived from the echo-path model, which can be subsequently mapped onto subjective estimates of customer perceived call quality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of novel structures for high order recursive digital filters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: This paper focuses on a novel filter structure, termed the 'parallel interconnection of cascade subfilters' (PICS) structure. The PICS structure is a structure which has been developed to overcome practical problems with the realisation of high order recursive filters. The benefits of this structure are discussed, and initial results from a practical investigation of filters realised with this structure are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of complex digital IIR filters with a finite number of samples
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: This paper deals with the design of a special type of digital IIR filters. These filters have complex coefficients and are designed to operate in the transient mode. The designed filters are suitable for differentiating between approaching and receding radar targets and rejecting clutter. The optimisation criteria is to approximate an ideal filter response while processing only a finite number of samples. Zero frequency initialisation is used as a predesign technique to enhance the clutter rejection capabilities of the complex filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel pipelining method for wave digital filters applied to carry ripple and carr wave techniques
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: This paper investigates the pipelining of a lattice wave digital filter composed of second order allpass sections implemented with twoport adaptors. Since it is a recursive structure, special care is required when pipelining is applied to achieve maximum clock and sample rates. A novel pipelining scheme, that exploits regularity of data flow, is presented and applied to the cases where carry ripple and carry save techniques are used in the implementation of the adaptor arithmetic. The results show improved sample rates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison study of SC biquads in the realisation of SC filters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: A systematic comparison for the realisation of SC filters using most popular SC biquads is given in this paper based on filter system realisation. Although the software has the facility to design a SC system with combined biquads, the authors restrict comparison to systems only composed of one kind of SC biquad, in order to simplify the question and make the guidelines of selecting SC biquads more practical for the SC filter designer who does not have SC compiler or has compiler but only with limited biquad structures. Comparison for SC filter realisation on total capacitance, capacitance spread, sensitivity, nonidealities and dynamic range is given. Some conclusions are obtained as very useful guidelines for the choice of a suitable biquad structure according to the nature of the filter problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved predistortion technique for active filters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: A powerful, analytically based and accurate procedure is described for predistorting the design of active filters affected by higher-frequency parasitics. The associated numerical algorithm enables all specified filter parameters to be established without solving complex nonlinear equations. The results are compared with those of other predistortion techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiplier-less FIR filter design with power-of-two coefficients
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: A novel approach for the design of optimum multiplier-less FIR filters is presented. This method is based on the sequential and modified sequential searching (pseudo-genetic evolutionary) methods. The proposed techniques are applicable to any filter type, and they do not pre-empt the architectures of the filter. The results have indicated their superior performances compared to the conventional methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital filter design using weighted least squares techniques
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: This paper describes techniques for designing IRR digital filters with arbitrary log-magnitude specifications. The techniques use iterative weighted least squares (WLS) methods to arrive at filters that are nearly optimal when measured on a logarithmic magnitude scale. The error weighting function is updated at each iteration and can be chosen to provide results that approximate the ideal response in a least squares or a minimax sense. A novel weight updating strategy is proposed, that provides some computational advantages. It is shown that certain simplifying approximations are good when the approximation error is small.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An alternative IMD prediction technique for active filters
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: Representing circuit variables in a frequency-domain complex matrix and nonlinearities by power series gives rise to an intermodulation-balance method. This operates entirely in the frequency domain and predicts IMD with accuracy and efficiency comparable to an alternative spectral-balance technique. The technique is verified for a single-amplifier filter example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An optimum jitter-minimising filter for optical fibre PPM synchronisation
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: Optical fibre pulse position modulation (PPM) synchronisation and sensitivity are considered under a jitter penalty. An optimum filter that minimises the sensitivity penalty due to the extracted PPM slot timing jitter is derived. The jitter sensitivity penalty is assessed in the absence of the optimum filter and when the filter is included. The selection of the PPM and phase lock loop (PLL) parameters that minimise the jitter is also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A direct approach to the design of multidimensional PCAS digital filters satisfying gain and group delay specifications simultaneously
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: Digital filters with linear or almost linear phase are required in many applications including video, sonar and image processing. A direct design approach is reported here which can be applied to 1-D and M-D filter design so long as the filter structure is a parallel combination of allpass subfilters (PCAS). PCAS filters are used because of their low complexity and roundoff noise as well as their ability to realise non-minimum phase transfer functions. The filter design will be shown to reduce to the solution of two sets of linear simultaneous equations. Examples are given in both the 1-D and 2-D case to illustrate the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new parameter set for digital filter representation
publicationTitle: 1993 IEE Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems (Digest No. 1993/199)
abstract: The choice of which parameter set to use will be determined partly by the design method. In this paper, three commonly used parameter sets are briefly examined in the context of digital-IIR filter design using optimization methods, in particular the method of simulated annealing. A new parameter set is then proposed which appears to possess some desirable properties, and an example is given illustrating the use of this new set in the design of a fourth-order filter by simulated annealing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
